title: Diarrhea
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with chronic foul-smelling, greasy diarrhea (steatorrhea), bloating, abdominal cramps, and weight loss. History reveals recent camping/hiking trip drinking untreated stream water. Giardia lamblia is a flagellated protozoan transmitted via fecal-oral route through contaminated water (common in hikers/campers — 'beaver fever'). Cysts are chlorine-resistant. Diagnosis: stool O&P (ova and parasites) — multiple samples needed (shedding intermittent). Stool Giardia antigen ELISA is more sensitive. String test (Entero-Test) if stool studies negative. Treatment: tinidazole (single dose) or metronidazole (5-7 days). Nitazoxanide for children. Paromomycin in pregnancy. Treat close contacts. Boil or filter water when camping.
chief_complaint: Chronic foul-smelling greasy diarrhea, bloating, weight loss
